meta-ethics|normative ethics|applied eth: The three branches of ethics: meta-ethics *discusses the meaning of terms and statements*, normative ethics *explores what moral norms one should follow*, applied ethics *examines what one ought to do in particular cases* (slide 10). See [Philosophy asks what science cannot answer, and ethics has three branches](#/libs7102-l1/philosophy-and-the-three-ethics).
no ought without can: *There can be no moral requirement to do something unless this is possible* (slide 14). See [Philosophy asks what science cannot answer, and ethics has three branches](#/libs7102-l1/philosophy-and-the-three-ethics).
no ought from is: *Moral value (what ought to be done) cannot ever be established from empirical facts (what is) alone*; an argument with only empirical premises and a value conclusion is incomplete and therefore invalid (slides 14, 29–30). See [Claims are empirical, value or conceptual, and a value conclusion needs a value premise](#/libs7102-l1/three-kinds-of-claim).
intrinsic value|instrumental value: Intrinsic value is value for its own sake; instrumental value is value as a means to something else; something can have both (slide 15). See [Philosophy asks what science cannot answer, and ethics has three branches](#/libs7102-l1/philosophy-and-the-three-ethics).
argument|premise|conclusion: *Persuasive structures containing statements with truth values: one or more premises and a conclusion*; premises are reasons to believe the conclusion; the argument itself is not a statement, so *there are no true or false arguments* (slide 16). See [Valid means the premises guarantee the conclusion; sound adds true premises](#/libs7102-l1/valid-and-sound).
valid|validity|truth-preserving: An argument is valid when *the truth of the premises guarantees the truth of the conclusion* (truth-preserving); it *can be valid regardless of whether the premises or conclusion are true* (slide 18). See [Valid means the premises guarantee the conclusion; sound adds true premises](#/libs7102-l1/valid-and-sound).
sound|soundness: An argument is sound *if and only if* it is valid and all its premises are true; validity is *a necessary but not sufficient condition for soundness* (slide 21). See [Valid means the premises guarantee the conclusion; sound adds true premises](#/libs7102-l1/valid-and-sound).
inductive argument|inductive leap: An attempt to generalize, such as *This anti-virus has been keeping my computer safe for years, so it's likely I will not get a virus this year*; never valid or invalid, only strong or weak (slide 17). See [Valid means the premises guarantee the conclusion; sound adds true premises](#/libs7102-l1/valid-and-sound).
empirical claim|value claim|conceptual c: Empirical: settled by sensory tests alone. Value: *a judgment of approval/disapproval that cannot be reduced to an empirical claim* (moral and aesthetic claims). Conceptual: settled by *the meaning of the words alone* (slide 28). See [Claims are empirical, value or conceptual, and a value conclusion needs a value premise](#/libs7102-l1/three-kinds-of-claim).
value argument|practical syllogism: An argument with *at least one value claim*, *one or more empirical claims, and a value conclusion*, after Aristotle: *All humans should exercise; I am a human being; I should exercise* (slide 29). See [Claims are empirical, value or conceptual, and a value conclusion needs a value premise](#/libs7102-l1/three-kinds-of-claim).
psychological egoism|normative egoism: Psychological egoism: *everyone is self-interested at all times (an empirical claim)*; normative egoism: *everyone ought to always act out of self-interest (a value/normative claim)* (slide 34). See [Self-interest is not selfishness, so genuine moral action exists](#/libs7102-l1/genuine-moral-action).
selfishness|self-interest: *Selfishness is excessive concern with one's self-interest*; not all self-interested actions are selfish, as tying your shoes or sleeping when tired shows (slide 39). See [Self-interest is not selfishness, so genuine moral action exists](#/libs7102-l1/genuine-moral-action).
